options.text: Creates a new commit that undoes the target commit's changes
Moves the branch pointer back to before the commit

questions.explanation: revert adds a new commit applying the inverse of the target, undoing its effect while leaving history intact — which is why it's safe on shared branches.

questions.prompt: Which `git reset` mode changes your working-tree files (and can discard uncommitted work)?

options.text: None of them touch the working tree

questions.explanation: --soft moves only the branch; --mixed also resets the staging area; --hard additionally resets the working tree, discarding uncommitted changes.

questions.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: git commit --amend replaces the previous commit with a new one
git reset --hard can permanently discard uncommitted changes
git restore --staged <file> unstages a file while keeping the edit
git revert deletes the target commit from history

questions.explanation: amend rewrites the last commit, reset --hard can lose uncommitted work, and restore --staged unstages. revert does not delete history — it adds an undo commit.

questions.prompt: To remove the last commit but keep its changes staged, run: git reset --______ HEAD~1
questions.explanation: git reset --soft HEAD~1 moves the branch back one commit but leaves the index and working tree untouched, so the changes remain staged.

questions.prompt: A commit you pushed yesterday is buggy, and teammates have already pulled it. What's the safest way to undo it?

options.text: git reset --hard to before the commit, then force-push
git revert the commit, creating a new undo commit
Delete the repository and start over

questions.explanation: revert adds a forward commit that undoes the change without rewriting shared history, so everyone stays in sync. reset/amend would rewrite history others already have.

questions.prompt: Match each command to its effect.

pairs.right: Discard unstaged edits to a file
Move the branch and discard working changes
Add a new commit that undoes a past one

questions.explanation: amend rewrites the last commit, restore discards working-tree edits, reset --hard is destructive, and revert is the safe, additive undo.
